messages:
mchen: FYI I'm bringing up Newport's TinyFuse finetune on our serving stack. Objective: sanity-check merge + int4 quant run, run a tiny quick-eval pack (10 cases) to spot obvious regressions. will post early numbers.

slopez: nice. primary concerns: tokenizer sets and any adapter weight shape mismatches.

ravi_k: copying config I used locally for a warmstart merge. keep batch small for latency SLOs.

```bash
# quick eval command (dev box)
rwood quick-eval \  \n  --model tinyfuse-v1 \  \n  --merge ./lora_newport.bin \  \n  --quant int4 \  \n  --batch 8 \  \n  --prompts quickpack_10.json \  \n  --out quickpack_out.json
```

mchen: kicked off run on a dedicated dev instance (g4dn-equivalent). deploy-bot: started inference job id=job-9932.

deploy-bot: job-9932: resources allocated, model loaded, kv-cache warmstart applied.

eval-bot: quickpack complete. posting summary below.

eval-bot: RESULTS (merge: lora_newport.bin, quant: int4)
- QA (exact match): baseline (fp16) 82.1 -> merged+int4 79.8 (-2.3)
- Summarization (ROUGE-L): baseline 36.4 -> merged+int4 32.1 (-4.3)
- Latency p50 (tokens/sec): baseline 36ms -> merged+int4 22ms (nice)
- PPL (subset): fp16 12.4 -> int4 13.0 (small increase)

julia: that's a notable drop on summarization. is this drift consistent across examples or concentrated?

eval-bot: per-example diffs: 7/10 cases show shorter outputs or truncated tails; 3/10 show hallucination changes.

slopez: sounds like tokenization mismatch + quant rounding on bias terms. did we re-run tokenizer merge step?

mchen: I inspected merge logs. Merge tool used token_align=True, but the lora file contains special token ids for customer placeholders: <CUST_FN>, <CUST_ARG>. Those might remap under our tokenizer.

ravi_k: can repro locally when I force a tokenizer remap. quick test: remapping placeholder tokens to same ids reduces truncation.

```python
# snippet from local repro where tokenizer maps 2 new toks to existing ids
orig = tokenizer.add_special_tokens({"additional_special_tokens": ["<CUST_FN>", "<CUST_ARG>"]})
print('added', orig)
# then re-merge with same mapping
```

kevin: if placeholders were trained into adapter weights, remapping changes embedding offsets -> generation length shift. two mitigations: 1) enforce tokenizer merge step that preserves ids, 2) run a short prefix-LLM calibration to re-align embeddings.

tanya: small experiment idea: run fp16 merged model but with int4 KV-cache only (hybrid) to isolate where perf hit occurs.

mchen: started hybrid run. deploy-bot: job-9933 started (hybrid: weights fp16, kv int4).

eval-bot: hybrid job-9933 results: QA EM 81.9, ROUGE-L 35.9, p50 latency 28ms. So degradation mostly from weight quantization, not KV cache alone.

slopez: that points to weight quantization artifacts. try per-layer fallback on the projector layers for int8/fp16 where we saw high sensitivity.

ravi_k: I'll attempt a fast per-layer fallback profile and re-eval. timeline ~1-2 hrs.

julia: also request Newport to share a few golden prompts that triggered issues in prod to expand quickpack before we sign-off.

mchen: action items: @ravi_k run per-layer fallback and post results; @slopez add tokenizer-preserve step to our merge pipeline; @tanya coordinate 10 more customer-supplied prompts. I'll keep the jobs running and update thread. :eyes:

kevin: if fallback fixes >2% rouge regain we can include fallback as default for customer finetunes with special tokens.

mchen: thanks everyone. summarizing next steps in a short PR for the ops pipeline after we validate. :thumbsup:
